On load, `AppProvider` (`apps/react-vite/src/app/provider.tsx`) wraps the whole app in `AuthLoader`, which comes from `configureAuth` in `apps/react-vite/src/lib/auth.tsx`. That loader calls `getUser`, which does `api.get('/auth/me')`. While it runs, a spinner shows. If the call succeeds, the user is stored in the query cache and `useUser()` returns it. `ProtectedRoute` in the same file (used by `app/router.tsx`) sends a user with no data to `/auth/login`, with the current path as `redirectTo`. `AuthLayout` (`src/components/layouts/auth-layout.tsx`) sends a signed-in user away from the sign-in and register pages to `redirectTo` or the dashboard. The request uses the shared Axios instance in `src/lib/api-client.ts`, which sends cookies (`withCredentials`). The session itself is a cookie that the API sets on login.

When any request fails, the response interceptor in `src/lib/api-client.ts` first shows an error toast with the server's message (or the Axios message). If the status is 401, it sets `window.location.href` to `paths.auth.login.getHref(redirectTo)`, where `paths` is in `src/config/paths.ts`. The promise is still rejected, so the calling query also sees the error. The redirect is a full page navigation, not a router navigation, and after sign-in `AuthLayout` returns the user to `redirectTo`.

I found two problems while reading this, and I did not run the app to confirm either one:

- **`redirectTo` is never read from the current URL.** The interceptor builds `new URLSearchParams()` empty, then reads `redirectTo` from it, so it always falls back to `window.location.pathname`. Any query string on the page is lost, so a user sent to sign-in from `/app/discussions?page=2` comes back to `/app/discussions`. The fix is to use `window.location.search`.
- **A 401 from `/auth/me` on the sign-in page may loop.** `AuthLoader` calls `/auth/me` on every page, including `/auth/login`. For a signed-out user that call returns 401, the interceptor sets the location to `/auth/login?redirectTo=/auth/login`, and the page reloads and repeats. The interceptor should skip the redirect for `/auth/me` or when the user is already on the sign-in page.

The mock API (`src/testing/mocks/handlers/auth.ts`, around line 152) returns 500, not 401, when `/auth/me` is called without a session. So in development the signed-out case never reaches the 401 redirect. It only goes through `ProtectedRoute`, and the user sees an error toast.
